archetype.name: Title Contender (defense-first, shorthanded)
archetype.definition: A recent champion-level team whose league-best defense keeps it among the elite even while two of its best players sit and its offense runs almost entirely through one guard.

report.headline: The league's best defense is carrying a shorthanded offense to 8-2
report.take:
Oklahoma City has opened 8-2 and sits atop the Northwest, and almost all of it comes from one end of the floor. The defensive rating of 105.5 ranks 1st in the league. The offense, at 113.6, ranks 18th and sits barely above the league average. That split is new. The last two seasons (68-14 and 64-18) paired a 1st-ranked defense with a top-seven offense. This version is still elite, but it is lopsided, and the sheet explains why: Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren have played three games each and are both listed Out, as is Jaylin Williams.

The defense is built on the rim. Opponents are shooting 55.5% within four feet against a league average of 65.2%, the best mark in the league, and their eFG % of 48.4 also ranks 1st. Opposing centers are scoring well below their usual output against this team, the biggest drop the league has allowed to the position. That is Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara doing the work without Holmgren, which is a strong sign. What the defense is not doing this year is forcing turnovers. Opp TOV % of 12.9 ranks 20th, down from 14.6 a year ago. This group wins by contesting shots, not by gambling for steals.

The offense is Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and not much else. He has 299 points at a 36.5 USG % with a BPM of 8.3. Ajay Mitchell (189 points, 58.8 TS %, +7.1 On-Off) has been the real second option. Beyond them the attack is thin. The 3PA Rate of 35.5 ranks 29th and the FT Rate of 23 ranks 27th, so the Thunder neither space the floor nor get to the line. They survive because they rarely give the ball away: their TOV % of 11.6 ranks 3rd. Jared McCain has soaked up 252 minutes at a 52.1 TS % and a -2.5 BPM, the minutes that Jalen Williams would normally take.

The record is honest. W vs Pt Diff is +1, so the margin supports about seven of the eight wins, and the 66-win pace reflects a real Net Rtg of 8.1 (5th). The trajectory is better than the 8-2 suggests. October was close to even on points, including blowout losses at Dallas and Houston. November has been 4-0 at 120.75 points scored and 100 allowed a game. If Holmgren and Jalen Williams return, the offense should climb back toward its usual level. A team with this defense and its past form is a contender even at its current site rank of 11th.

strengths.title: League-best rim protection
strengths.body: Opponents are shooting far below the league average at the rim and posting the league's lowest eFG %, and that has held up with Holmgren out. Some of it will regress: rim percentage is noisy over 10 games, and last season's mark was 59.6. But the scheme has produced a 1st-ranked defense three straight seasons, so this is a foundation, not a fluke.

strengths.title: Ball security keeps the offense afloat
strengths.body: A TOV % of 11.6, 3rd in the league, means a below-average shooting team still gets a full set of shots every night. It fits the franchise's history of low turnover rates and a ball-dominant star who rarely gives it away. Expect it to last.

strengths.title: Gilgeous-Alexander and Mitchell up top
strengths.body: The backcourt grades B+ on the strength of a star posting an 8.3 BPM and a second guard with the best On-Off on the roster. Mitchell's efficiency has given the Thunder a real secondary creator while the wings and frontcourt are depleted.

concerns.title: A narrow, one-man offense
concerns.body: An 18th-ranked ORtg comes from low volume from three, few free throws and a 22nd-ranked eFG %. It is well below the top-seven offenses of recent seasons. It is mostly caused by injuries, so it should improve once the missing pieces return. Until then, any off night from Gilgeous-Alexander leaves little to fall back on.

concerns.title: Missing wings and stretch big
concerns.body: The only listed wing is Jalen Williams, Out after three games. Holmgren, the frontcourt's best-ranked player, is also Out, which helps explain the C frontcourt grade. Their minutes have gone to McCain's inefficient shooting and to reserves with deeply negative On-Off numbers.

concerns.title: Some defensive luck from three
concerns.body: Opponents are hitting 32.6% from three, well under last season's 36.9%, while the defense is forcing fewer turnovers than it used to. When the three-point luck evens out, the defense will look more like very good than untouchable.

trend.note: October was a near-even 4-2 with two blowout road losses; November is 4-0 with the offense jumping to 120.75 points a game, and the last five have run well above the season margin.

weekAhead.headline: Four road games, opening with a Portland back-to-back
weekAhead.body:
The whole week is on the road, and it front-loads the hardest part. Portland is 6-3 and 3rd on the site with a 4th-ranked offense. It takes threes and draws fouls at among the league's highest rates, which directly tests whether Oklahoma City's rim-first defense can hold up when opponents shoot from outside and get to the line. Portland's defense is also strongest exactly where the Thunder attack: point guards and shooting guards fall well below their usual production against the Blazers. Playing them on consecutive nights is the real challenge of the week.

The back half is much softer. The Clippers (2-7) give up big games to shooting guards and turn the ball over constantly. Sacramento (1-9, 29th on the site) has the league's worst rim defense. A split in Portland and two wins would be a good week; a sweep of the trip would confirm the November form.

keyMatchups.title: Thunder guards vs Portland's perimeter defense
keyMatchups.body: Portland holds shooting guards and point guards well under their usual output, ranking among the league's best on both. With the offense running through Gilgeous-Alexander and Mitchell, that is a direct clash with the Thunder's only reliable scoring.

keyMatchups.title: Portland's threes and free throws
keyMatchups.body: Portland's high 3PA Rate and FT Rate pull the game away from the rim, where Oklahoma City's defense does its best work. The Blazers' A- frontcourt also makes them one of the stiffer interior tests on the schedule.

keyMatchups.title: Soft landing in LA and Sacramento
keyMatchups.body: The Clippers rank 29th in TOV % and allow the most production to shooting guards, which suits Mitchell. Sacramento allows a 75% rim FG %, last in the league, which should help an offense that otherwise struggles to create easy shots.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the Thunder's offense can produce anything beyond Gilgeous-Alexander against Portland's guard-smothering defense on the second night of the back-to-back.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense is the sustainable part. Three straight seasons of elite defense say the rim protection and shot contests are structural, even if the opponents' three-point and rim percentages drift back toward normal and the defensive rating rises somewhat. The offense is the part with upside. It is running well below its usual level with two core players out, and their return would take touches from McCain and the struggling reserves. That is the path back to a Net Rtg around 10.

Nothing in the record is inflated by close games, so the main risk is health rather than regression. A finish around 58 to 63 wins is the reasonable range. The low end assumes extended absences; the high end assumes the offense climbs back into the league's top ten.
swingFactors: Return of Chet Holmgren and Jalen Williams
How far opponent rim and three-point shooting regress

confidence.note: Only 10 games, with key players out for most of them.
